title: Caching Strategies
description: Cache placement, read/write patterns (cache-aside, write-through, write-behind, write-around), invalidation approaches, and the three named failure modes: thundering herd, penetration, avalanche.
viz: toggle between cache-aside/write-through/write-behind/write-around request flows animated through client to cache to DB, plus a thundering-herd stampede simulator with a single-flight lock toggle showing concurrent DB hits collapse from N to 1

title: Queues and Backpressure
description: Work queues vs event logs, delivery guarantees (at-least-once plus idempotency), per-key ordering, and backpressure mechanisms that keep overload from silently turning into unbounded latency.
viz: animated producer/consumer queue with adjustable production rate vs consumer pool size showing consumer lag grow under a 5x burst; bounded-queue toggle demonstrating backpressure kicking in vs an unbounded queue growing without limit

title: Consistency Trade-offs
description: CAP restated correctly via PACELC, the consistency spectrum (strong/sequential/causal/eventual), session guarantees, database isolation levels, and quorum math (W+R>N).
viz: PACELC decision tree with a partition toggle (choose A or C) and a normal-operation toggle (choose L or C), plus a quorum simulator with N/W/R sliders showing whether W+R>N holds and whether a stale read becomes possible

title: Sharding and Partitioning
description: Range vs hash vs consistent-hash partitioning, shard-key selection criteria, the noisy-neighbour problem, fixed-partition-count rebalancing, and local vs global secondary indexes.
viz: ring diagram for consistent hashing showing keys and nodes as points on a circle, add/remove-node buttons animating how few keys remap, contrasted with a hash-mod-N toggle showing nearly all keys remapping on the same operation

title: Idempotency
description: Why at-least-once delivery makes idempotency non-negotiable, the idempotency-key pattern (client-generated, atomic check-and-store), natural idempotency via conditional writes, and HTTP method semantics.
viz: animated request-retry sequence showing a client retry with the same idempotency key hitting a stored-response short-circuit, contrasted with a naive endpoint double-executing (double charge) when the key is regenerated per attempt

title: Circuit Breakers and Bulkheads
description: Circuit breaker states (closed/open/half-open) and required fallback behavior, bulkheads as resource partitioning to limit blast radius, and the supporting cast: timeouts, jittered backoff, retry budgets.
viz: state machine diagram (closed/open/half-open) with a failure-rate slider driving transitions, plus a bulkhead panel showing separate thread pools per dependency where one pool exhausting doesn't starve the others, compared to a shared-pool scenario cascading

title: Change Data Capture (CDC)
description: Why dual writes aren't atomic, log-based CDC off the replication log (WAL/binlog/oplog) vs trigger-based vs query-based, and the transactional outbox pattern for explicit event-schema control.
viz: side-by-side animated diagram: dual-write anti-pattern showing a crash between the two writes leaving DB and event bus permanently inconsistent, vs CDC reading the replication log producing an exactly-committed event stream, with a transactional-outbox variant toggle

title: Rate Limiting
description: Protection vs compliance limiting, algorithm comparison (token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed/sliding window), distributed rate limiting across a fleet, and cost-based limiting for variable-cost requests.
viz: token bucket visualizer with refill-rate and bucket-size sliders showing burst absorption, plus an algorithm selector cycling through token bucket / leaky bucket / fixed window (showing the boundary-doubling exploit) / sliding window counter

title: Load Balancing
description: L4 vs L7 load balancing, algorithm choice (round robin, least connections, consistent hashing, weighted), health checks, and connection draining during deploys.
viz: traffic distribution simulator across backend instances with an algorithm selector (round robin/least-conn/consistent-hash), a slow/unhealthy instance toggle showing health-check ejection, and connection draining animated during a rolling restart

title: Service Discovery
description: Client-side vs server-side service discovery, DNS-based discovery, and service registries (Consul, etcd, ZooKeeper) — how services find each other as instances scale up and down.
viz: animated service registry with instances registering/deregistering via heartbeat, client-side discovery calling the registry directly vs server-side discovery via a load balancer/sidecar, showing stale-endpoint risk when a heartbeat lags

title: Consensus Algorithms (Raft/Paxos)
description: Leader election and distributed consensus — how a cluster agrees on a single value despite node failures, why majority quorums prevent split-brain, and why consensus is expensive and reserved for metadata rather than data-plane traffic.
viz: animated Raft cluster with leader election triggered on node failure, log replication requiring a majority quorum before commit, and a network-partition toggle showing split-brain prevented because only the majority side can elect a leader

title: Database Replication
description: Leader-follower vs multi-leader vs leaderless replication, synchronous vs asynchronous replication, replication lag, and failover mechanics when a follower falls behind or a leader dies.
viz: replication topology selector (single-leader/multi-leader/leaderless) with an adjustable network-delay slider showing replication lag grow, a leader-failure button triggering failover, and a conflicting-write scenario in multi-leader mode

title: Distributed Transactions (2PC & Saga)
description: Two-phase commit and its coordinator-blocking failure mode, the Saga pattern (choreography vs orchestration) with compensating actions, TCC, and why atomic multi-service transactions are avoided in practice.
viz: animated 2PC prepare/commit sequence across three services with a coordinator-crash-after-prepare failure mode leaving participants blocked, contrasted with a Saga executing sequential steps and running compensating actions when a later step fails

title: Concurrency Control (Optimistic, Pessimistic, MVCC)
description: Optimistic vs pessimistic locking, and multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) — how databases let readers and writers avoid blocking each other, and when optimistic locking's retry cost bites.
viz: two concurrent transactions editing the same row: pessimistic mode shows one transaction blocking on a lock, optimistic mode shows a version-check conflict and retry, MVCC mode shows each transaction reading its own consistent snapshot without blocking

title: Distributed Locking and Fencing Tokens
description: Distributed locks (Redlock, lease-based locks) and why a naive lock built on a single key is dangerous under GC pauses or clock drift, and how fencing tokens close the gap between lock expiry and actual work completion.
viz: two clients racing for a distributed lock with an adjustable GC-pause/clock-drift slider showing a lock expiring mid-critical-section and a second client acquiring it; a fencing-token toggle shows the stale client's late write rejected downstream

title: Event Sourcing and CQRS
description: Storing state as an append-only sequence of events and separating write models from read models (CQRS) — rebuilding current state by replay, and the operational cost of eventual consistency between the two sides.
viz: event log accumulating append-only events with a replay button rebuilding current state from scratch, alongside a CQRS diagram showing writes going to the command model while a projector asynchronously updates a separate read-optimized view

title: Observability (Metrics, Logs, Traces)
description: The three pillars — metrics, logs, and distributed traces — plus SLIs/SLOs/SLAs and error budgets, and how they compose to answer 'is the system healthy' and 'why did this one request fail.'
viz: a single request flowing through four services rendered as a distributed trace waterfall (spans with latency), paired with an SLO burn-rate gauge showing the error budget being consumed faster during a simulated incident

title: API Design and Evolution
description: REST vs gRPC vs GraphQL tradeoffs, backward-compatible schema evolution, and pagination strategies (offset vs cursor-based) — designing APIs that can change without breaking existing clients.
viz: API style comparison panel (REST/gRPC/GraphQL) showing the same request represented in each, a schema-evolution timeline showing an added-vs-removed field breaking old clients, and an offset-vs-cursor pagination simulator under concurrent inserts

title: Indexing and Storage Engines (B-tree vs LSM-tree)
description: B-tree vs LSM-tree storage engines — why B-trees favor read-heavy in-place-update workloads and LSM-trees favor write-heavy workloads via compaction, and how this drives database engine choice.
viz: side-by-side animated write path: a B-tree performing in-place page updates vs an LSM-tree appending to a memtable/SSTable with background compaction merging levels, plus a read-amplification vs write-amplification comparison readout

title: Zero-Downtime Deployments
description: Blue-green, canary, and rolling deployment strategies, plus the expand-contract pattern for safe schema migrations — shipping changes without a maintenance window or a broken in-flight request.
viz: deployment strategy selector (blue-green/canary/rolling) animating traffic shifting across old and new instance pools, with an error-rate spike triggering an automatic rollback when in canary mode

title: Multi-Region Architecture
description: Active-active vs active-passive multi-region designs, cross-region latency, data residency constraints, and conflict resolution (last-write-wins, CRDTs) when the same data is writable in two regions.
viz: two-region diagram with an adjustable cross-region latency slider; an active-active toggle shows concurrent writes to the same key in both regions with a CRDT merge resolving the conflict, vs a last-write-wins toggle silently dropping one write

title: Connection Pooling and Resource Exhaustion
description: Connection pool sizing, exhaustion, and the counterintuitive failure mode where increasing pool size makes an overloaded database worse — pool-per-dependency as a bulkhead, and external pooling (PgBouncer-style).
viz: adjustable pool-size slider against a fixed downstream DB capacity showing queueing latency first improve then collapse past the DB's true capacity, illustrating why 'just increase the pool' backfires
